en: Mount Mayon in Albay is famous for having the most perfect cone shape among all active volcanoes in the Philippines.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers through the Cagayan Valley region.
The Philippine tarsier, found in Bohol, is one of the world's smallest primates and has enormous eyes adapted for night hunting.
Taal Lake in Batangas surrounds Volcano Island, which contains a smaller inner body of water known as Main Crater Lake.
Mount Apo in Mindanao is the highest peak in the Philippines, reaching an elevation of 2,954 meters above sea level.
The Philippines produces abaca, a species of banana plant whose strong fibers are used worldwide to make durable ropes and paper.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a UNESCO World Heritage site protecting hundreds of coral and fish species.
The Philippines experiences the amihan, a cool northeast monsoon from November to February, and the habagat, a warm southwest monsoon bringing heavy rains.
Palawan is the longest and narrowest province in the Philippines, stretching over 400 kilometers between the South China Sea and the Sulu Sea.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River National Park in Palawan features an eight-kilometer underground river that flows directly into the sea.
The critically endangered Philippine eagle, the national bird, primarily preys on colugos, monkeys, and large reptiles in the forests of Mindanao.
The Cordillera Administrative Region in northern Luzon contains the famous Banaue Rice Terraces, which were carved into the mountains by the Ifugao people.
